summary: In the staircase, Morpheus looks up the stairs as he hears a helicopter and urges the others on: "Come on!" Apoc slaps a gun into Neo's hand, saying it is "Something to ward off evil spirits." Neo nods and stuffs the gun into his belt.

what_changes.before: Neo is unarmed on the staircase as the group moves under threat.
what_changes.after: Neo is armed, having taken a gun to defend himself.
what_changes.evidence: Apoc slaps a gun into Neo's hand.

event_hint.one_line: The crew hurries up the staircase, arming themselves as a helicopter closes in.

minds.wants: To get the group moving up the stairs and out of the building before the helicopter's occupants locate them.
minds.feels: Heightened, focused alarm. The helicopter sound confirms the glitch/deja-vu was not a minor error but a serious breach — the trap Tank has just identified on the main deck. He is already converting that recognition into command rather than letting it become panic.
minds.shows: A single upward glance and a two-word imperative — 'Come on!' — with no explanation and no visible fear. He gives direction, not reassurance.
minds.basis: He looks up the stairs the instant he hears the helicopter and immediately urges the others forward. In sc-093 he was quietly listening to the building while Trinity explained the deja-vu as a Matrix glitch, so he has been tracking the threat building; now it has arrived as a sound. His command is terse and forward-pushing, consistent with a leader who has judged there is no time to talk.

believes_about.belief: That Apoc will handle arming the group without needing to be told, so Morpheus can devote himself entirely to movement and timing.

minds.wants: To get a weapon into Neo's hand fast and make him ready to fight, while keeping his own nerve steady enough to do it.
minds.feels: Adrenaline mixed with a jolt of dark humor — the kind of joke you make precisely because the situation is frightening. The wisecrack is a way of managing his own fear and of treating Neo as one of the crew rather than a liability in a moment that demands everyone pull weight.
minds.shows: A brisk physical gesture — slapping the gun into Neo's palm — paired with a glib line about 'evil spirits.' He performs casual competence; nothing about the dread underneath is visible.
minds.basis: He arms Neo rather than hesitating, and his line reframes a lethal weapon as a folk charm against 'evil spirits' — gallows humor that only surfaces under genuine threat. This is the crew's first arming-up under the helicopter, so his flippancy reads as a coping mechanism rather than true ease.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is still green enough to need a joke to steady him and to be handed a weapon rather than expected to have one ready himself.

minds.wants: To accept the weapon and be ready — to stop being the unprotected newcomer and become someone who can contribute to the crew's survival.
minds.feels: A sober, quickening realization that the abstract danger he's been warned about is now concrete and closing in. The deja-vu and the helicopter have collapsed the distance between the story he was told and the reality he is now in; he is afraid but resolving rather than freezing.
minds.shows: A single nod and a practical motion — stuffing the gun into his belt. He offers no joke back and no visible fear; he simply takes the weapon and makes himself ready, matching Morpheus's terse urgency.
minds.basis: He accepts the gun without question and immediately stows it for use, an action that marks a shift from the man who, in the Oracle's apartment (ev-021), was told he is 'not the One' and must choose between lives. The nod is acknowledgment, not ease; paired with the belt-stowing, it shows him converting fear into readiness rather than performing either panic or bravado.

believes_about.belief: That Apoc's joke means the situation is under some control and that a weapon is a token of belonging as much as a tool.

connects_back: sc-093: Trinity identifies the deja-vu (black cat) as a Matrix glitch that occurs 'when they change something,' and the helicopter blades grow ominously loud — this scene delivers the consequence of that change.
sc-094: Tank's realization 'It's a trap!' on the main deck is the off-screen cause of the helicopter's arrival and the crew's need to arm and move.
ev-021: Neo's verdict as 'not the One' and the instruction to keep it secret frame his quiet, unprotesting acceptance of a weapon he has not yet earned a reputation for using.
sets_up: ev-022: The armed, hurried crew reaching the Hotel Lafayette where the Agents brick up the windows and a firefight/Mouse's death follows — the guns Apoc distributes here are the ones they will use.
ev-023: The escape and extraction run that requires the crew to be armed and moving under pursuit.
ev-026/027: Neo's later willingness to lead a rescue assault and engage in a firefight — his arming here is the first step in becoming someone who takes up weapons rather than being protected.
dramatic_function: To convert the abstract warning of a Matrix glitch into immediate, physical peril — arming the crew and setting them in motion so the story shifts from prophecy and dread (the Oracle) into the chase and combat that follow, while quietly marking Neo's transition from protected candidate to an active, weapon-bearing participant.
